clue.text: Imagine wild cat regularly peered around

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
turning around means facing the other way, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: a puma is a big cat living in the wild
the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone pictures a wild cat that keeps peering round at them.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces at once, not just the second; 'cat' wants to be the definition, but 'Imagine' at the front is.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream something up is to invent it in the mind, a phrasal-verb synonym of picturing or conceiving.

clue.text: Stand-up moving cleaner’s equipment

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the hyphenated word, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A stand-up comedian's act involving a cleaner's kit being carried about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand-up' reads as a comedian, but it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the flat scoop a household cleaner sweeps dirt into, one item of their kit.

clue.text: Messaged English servant about French article

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
a maid is a female household servant
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A note sent to an English housemaid concerning an item in a French paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French article' looks like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article, the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have emailed someone is to have sent them an electronic message, a direct synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: A pair of notes about copy

blocks.note: two of the sol-fa note mi
c, for circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Two memos written regarding a duplicate document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but here simply gives C, from Latin circa, used with approximate dates.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to imitate someone, a straightforward verb synonym for reproducing their actions or voice.

clue.text: Soppy Romanian harbours burning desire

indicators.note: a harbour shelters ships within it, so the phrase shelters the solution inside its letters

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A sentimental man from Romania secretly nurses a passionate longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning desire' reads as a cliché for passion, but it is literal: a compulsion to set fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is the psychiatric compulsion to start fires, so literally an urge for things to be ablaze.

clue.text: Miser‘s self-regard or empty callousness returned

indicators.note: an empty word has had its contents scooped out, leaving only its two ends
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the ego is one's sense of self-importance
taken as written
first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A miser is accused of vanity or of hardness of heart that comes back hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Miser' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; the reversal covers all three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, the tight-fisted moneylender of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, became a byword for any stingy person.

clue.text: American revolutionary ultimately obtained visa again for country

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are turned to face backwards
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A US rebel finally gets a fresh visa to enter a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American revolutionary' suggests a figure such as Paul Revere, but 'revolutionary' just turns US round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa, so it is one example of a country.

clue.text: Doctor runs over prodding Tom perhaps in complicated procedure

indicators.note: to prod is to poke into something, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: to doctor results is to rig or falsify them
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a tom is a male cat, so tom is an example of a male

explanation.surface: A doctor runs across and prods a patient called Tom during a fiddly operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician or an anagram signal, but it is a verb meaning rig; RO pokes into MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tiresome and needlessly elaborate process, the same idea as a convoluted procedure.

clue.text: Best stone worn by Henman?

indicators.note: something worn is wrapped around the wearer, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: an opal is a gemstone
Tim Henman was a leading British tennis player; the question mark flags a name given by example

explanation.surface: Asking whether the finest gem was the one the tennis player wore.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was Britain's top male tennis player around 2000; the gem goes round his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal describes the most favourable or effective option, so it is an adjectival synonym of best.

clue.text: Two hesitant expressions encapsulating traitor’s mistake

indicators.note: a capsule encloses its contents, so the outer pieces wrap round an inner one

blocks.note: er and um are both noises of hesitation
a rat is slang for someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Stammering noises reveal that a turncoat has slipped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The two hesitations sit either side of RAT; the 's after 'traitor' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printed or written work, often listed in a correction slip.

clue.text: Conman Mark visited by Madame

indicators.note: a place visited has someone come inside it, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
Mme is the written abbreviation of the French title Madame

explanation.surface: A swindler named Mark receives a call from a French lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a man's name alongside 'Conman', but it is the common noun meaning scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A scammer is someone who runs fraudulent schemes to cheat people, the modern word for a confidence trickster.

clue.text: Bright light in the sky troubles sailor

blocks.note: bad luck that dogs you troubles you
tar, short for tarpaulin, is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A strange glow overhead worries a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' reads as a noun but is the verb dogs, as in a problem that dogs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dog Star is Sirius, the brightest star seen in the night sky, in the constellation Canis Major.

clue.text: Officer parking by new coalmine

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer leaving the car next to a newly opened pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places P beside the rearranged letters, rather than meaning 'next to' in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman is a police officer, the uniformed member of the force the word officer often names.

clue.text: Confess Cambridge University’s on notice

blocks.note: an ad is a notice advertising something
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: An academic owns up that a Cambridge college has been given notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge University' points to England, but the institute meant is in Cambridge, Massachusetts; 'on' puts it after the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a fault is to own up to it, a direct verb synonym of confessing.

clue.text: Northern guys ignoring lead sculptures out of habit?

indicators.note: to ignore the lead is to leave off whatever comes first

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for northern
dudes is slang for guys

explanation.surface: Men up north overlook the leading role and carve statues from routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of habit' suggests routine, but a habit is also clothing, as worn by a nun; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudes are statues of unclothed figures, and being out of one's habit means wearing no garments.

clue.text: Newspaper employee hopeful lover’s collecting cot

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: a suitor is a man courting a woman in hope of marriage
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A journalist's would-be sweetheart picks up a baby's crib.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has', so the suitor has the cot inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor checks and corrects copy and writes headlines on a newspaper, a role on its staff.

clue.text: Number for Spice Girl making a comeback? That’s fine!

indicators.note: a comeback is a return journey, so the letters travel back the other way

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
to be pro something is to be for it
Mel B, Scary Spice, was one of the Spice Girls pop group

explanation.surface: A song written for a reunited Spice Girl, greeted with approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' suggests a song, but gives NO; Mel B, Melanie Brown, was one of the 1990s British girl group.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No problem!' is a casual reply signalling agreement or that something is acceptable, like 'That's fine!'

clue.text: Gerry’s backing musician showing a bit of heart

blocks.note: first meaning: a member of the 1960s Liverpool band that backed the singer Gerry Marsden
second meaning: the cluster of cells that sets the heartbeat

explanation.surface: A band member who backed a singer named Gerry shows some courage or warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerry and the Pacemakers were a Merseybeat band fronted by Gerry Marsden, famous for You'll Never Walk Alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinoatrial node, the natural rhythm-setting tissue of the heart, is called its pacemaker, as is the band member.

clue.text: Gaelic bar cryptically using symbols instead of numbers

indicators.note: something written cryptically is scrambled into code, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish pub sign written in code, with symbols where the figures should be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first half is fodder; 'cryptically' is the only signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra represents quantities with letters and signs such as x and y, rather than specific figures.

clue.text: Embarrassed and humbled touring hospital

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all round it, so one piece circles the other

blocks.note: to be abased is to be humiliated or lowered in dignity
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A red-faced, humiliated visitor being shown round a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'touring' wraps the humbled word round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abashed is to feel ashamed and self-conscious, a near synonym for being made to blush.

clue.text: Thought visitor outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken words are said aloud, so the solution is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a guest is a visitor, and the word said aloud matches the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone reckoned a caller was blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' reads as frank, describing the visitor, but it marks the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Guessed means supposed or estimated, so it matches thought in the sense of believed without certainty.

clue.text: Board members and former partners retaining copyright

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of within, so one piece is kept inside another

blocks.note: exes are former spouses or partners
C is the copyright symbol, the circled letter

explanation.surface: Company directors and their ex-wives keep hold of the rights to a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two halves; the exes hold the copyright symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Execs is short for executives, the senior managers who sit on a company's governing board.

clue.text: Graceful eastern soldier holding on

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it clasped inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for eastern
a soldier ant is a caste of ant, so ant is crossword shorthand for soldier
the on side and the leg side are the same half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A refined soldier from the East clinging on.
explanation.walkthrough: The eastern soldier is a two-part outer piece that holds 'on'; in cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes stylish poise and refinement in movement or appearance, a close synonym of graceful.

clue.text: Last kid swimming for island group

indicators.note: things swimming about move freely and lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The final child to swim out to an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: St Kilda is a remote archipelago off the west coast of Scotland, abandoned by its people in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: St Kilda is a cluster of small islands and stacks in the Atlantic, west of the Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Change a minute tip

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: Alter a tiny piece of advice, or a small gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like the adjective tiny, but it is the unit of time, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to make alterations to it, a verb synonym of change.

clue.text: Cut strange, extremely porous wood

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters survive

blocks.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
first and last letters only
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Someone saws a timber that is oddly full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb about the wood, but it is the noun: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump steak is a cut of beef taken from the hindquarters, so it is one butcher's cut.

clue.text: Scares unclothed Conservative

indicators.note: stripping off clothes removes the outer layer, so the outermost letters go and the inside stays

blocks.note: frights, with the first and last letters stripped off

explanation.surface: A naked Tory gives people a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: Scares is the noun frights; drop its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The political right is the conservative side, so a Conservative is someone of the right.

clue.text: Small involuntary movement after receiving Oscar for Marcus Aurelius?

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for small
a tic is an involuntary twitch
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tiny twitch after winning an Academy Award, said to be fit for a Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places TIC after S, and 'receiving' puts O inside TIC; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius wrote the Meditations and is the best-known follower of Stoic philosophy.

clue.text: Husband aghast, changing social media feature

indicators.note: letters that are changing take on a new form and order

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband horrified by a change to his social media account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' sits between the fodder and the definition and could be read with either.
explanation.definitionFit: A hashtag is a word preceded by the # symbol used to tag and group posts online.

clue.text: Smartypants with Kelvin these days barely calls

indicators.note: something bare has had its covering stripped away, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin temperature unit
these days means at present, now
the inner letters once the first and last go

explanation.surface: A clever-clogs named Kelvin hardly ever phones nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kelvin' reads as a man's name, but it is the unit symbol K; 'barely' strips calls to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who behaves as though they understand everything, an irritating clever person.

clue.text: French philosopher produced rent, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters are mirrored

blocks.note: to do something is to produce it, as in did a drawing
rent is the past tense of rend, meaning tore

explanation.surface: A French thinker, after some thought, came up with money for the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like housing payment, but it is the old past tense of rend, tore.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was the eighteenth-century French Enlightenment thinker who edited the great Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Apricot tagine includes cheese

indicators.note: to include is to contain within, so the phrase contains the solution in its letters

blocks.note: runs from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A Moroccan apricot stew with some cheese stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole scene is a recipe, which hides the join between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft, fresh Italian whey cheese often used in cooking and desserts.
